# Aster

> Aster is a tiny, browser-native, zero-VDOM web framework powered by JavaScript Generator Components (`function*` / `async function*`), Slot-Compiled `<template>` Patching, Unified Web Components (`defineElement`), and Automatic Event-Delegated Lazy Revival — built on Vite+ (`vp`) with zero runtime dependencies and zero backend opinions.

## Rules for AI Coding Assistants (Read First)

1. **NEVER use React hooks or VDOM patterns:** No `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `useRef`, or `React.Fragment`.
2. **NEVER use Solid/Vue reactivity boilerplate for local state:** No `() =>` JSX thunks, no `<Show>` / `<For>`, no `.value`, and no `$state` / `$derived` runes.
3. **Stateful components are `function*` generators:** Declare local state with plain `let`, run setup before the loop, and yield JSX inside `for (props of ctx)` (or `for (;;)` if the component takes no props).
4. **Always use `for (props of ctx)` when reading `props`:** Writing `for (;;)` freezes `props` at initial mount; forgetting the loop causes the generator to exit (`done: true`) after the first render.
5. **Stateless components are plain `function`s:** Zero generator allocation and 0 bytes of client JS in SSR.
6. **Cleanup uses native `try { ... } finally { ... }`:** Triggered automatically via `gen.return()` on unmount.
7. **Shared client state uses `signal()`:** Read via `sig()`, write via `sig.set(next)` or `sig.update(fn)`. Reading inside a `function*` auto-subscribes that component.
8. **SSR-safe subtree state uses Context:** Use `createContext()`, `provide()`, `useContext()`, or `<Provider>` so concurrent server requests never share module-level state.
9. **Lazy Revival is 100% automatic:** NEVER wrap components in `island()` or `$` syntax. Any `export function*` is automatically stamped with `__asterSrc` by `@fierst/aster/vite`.
10. **Routing uses plain `<a href="/...">` tags:** NEVER import or invent a `<Link>` component. `<Router>` intercepts same-origin links natively via the browser Navigation API + `URLPattern` + View Transitions.
11. **External push updates need `ctx.refresh()`:** Event handlers (`onClick`, `onSubmit`, `bind:*`, and child `on*` callbacks) auto-refresh; external timers (`setInterval`, `WebSocket`) call `ctx.refresh()`.
    For focus or native dialogs, use `ref={el => ctx.afterRender(() => el.focus())}`. The callback runs once after the owning component's next successful client DOM patch. Registration does not schedule a render. SSR skips it.
12. **Native 2026 HTML controls are built-in:** Use `<dialog closedby="any">`, `popover`, `popovertarget`, `commandfor`, `command`, `scope` (`@scope`), and `css` (`CSSStyleSheet`).

## Core API Quick Reference

### Imports
- `@fierst/aster`: `render`, `claim`, `signal`, `createContext`, `provide`, `useContext`, `Provider`, `ErrorBoundary`, `defineElement`, `css`, `scope`, `html`, `type Ctx`
- `@fierst/aster/router`: `Router`, `navigate`, `matchRoute`, `useLocation`, `useParams`, `useSearchParams`, `type RouteDef`
- `@fierst/aster/ssr`: `renderToString`, `renderToStringAsync`, `renderDocument`, `htmlResponse`, `renderToStream`, `streamResponse`, `resolveIslandSrc`
- `@fierst/aster/revive`: `installRevival`
- `@fierst/aster/vite`: `aster` (default export Vite+ plugin)
- `@fierst/aster/astro`: `asterAstro` (default export Astro integration supporting `client:load`, `client:idle`, `client:visible`, `client:media`, `client:only`)

### Canonical Stateful Component (`function*`)
```tsx
import { type Ctx } from '@fierst/aster';

export function* Counter(props: { start?: number; label?: string }, ctx: Ctx) {
  let count = props.start ?? 0;

  for (props of ctx) {
    const doubled = count * 2;
    yield (
      <button onClick={() => count++}>
        {props.label ?? 'Clicks'}: {count} (2x = {doubled})
      </button>
    );
  }
}
```

### Two-Way Form Bindings, Directives, & Keyed Lists
```tsx
export function* TodoList() {
  let draft = '';
  const items = [{ id: '1', title: 'Ship Aster', done: false }];

  const add = (e: SubmitEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (!draft.trim()) return;
    items.unshift({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), title: draft.trim(), done: false });
    draft = '';
  };

  for (;;) {
    yield (
      <section>
        <form onSubmit={add}>
          <input bind:value={draft} placeholder="New task..." />
          <button disabled={!draft.trim()}>Add</button>
        </form>
        <ul>
          {items.map((item) => (
            <li key={item.id}>
              <input type="checkbox" bind:checked={item.done} />
              <span class:done={item.done}>{item.title}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </section>
    );
  }
}
```

### Composable Multi-Step UI Flows (`yield*`)
```tsx
function* confirmDelete(title: string) {
  let choice: boolean | null = null;
  while (choice === null) {
    yield (
      <div role="alertdialog">
        <span>Delete {title}?</span>
        <button onClick={() => (choice = false)}>Cancel</button>
        <button onClick={() => (choice = true)}>Confirm</button>
      </div>
    );
  }
  return choice;
}
```

Use synchronous generators for interactive delegated steps. Async generators automatically advance after each yield and should produce finite sequences. Pass a const signal directly to `bind:value`, or supply a mutable local or `[get, set]` pair. Return promises from event handlers for error boundary handling.

### Async Components (`async function*`) & Cancellation
```tsx
export async function* UserProfile(props: { id: string }, ctx: Ctx) {
  yield <p>Loading #{props.id}...</p>;
  const res = await fetch(`/api/users/${props.id}`, { signal: ctx.signal });
  const user = await res.json();
  yield <h2>{user.name}</h2>;
}
```
Note: `async function*` automatically aborts `ctx.signal` and restarts whenever `props` change.

### Unified Web Components (`defineElement`)
```tsx
import { defineElement, css } from '@fierst/aster';
import { Counter } from './Counter.tsx';

defineElement('aster-counter', Counter, {
  props: { start: 'number', label: 'string' },
  shadow: true,
  styles: css`button { border-radius: 999px; }`,
});
```

### Streaming SSR & Automatic Lazy Revival
```ts
import manifest from './dist/aster-manifest.json' with { type: 'json' };
import { streamResponse } from '@fierst/aster/ssr';
import { App } from './app.tsx';

export default {
  fetch(req: Request) {
    const url = new URL(req.url);
    return streamResponse(<App url={url.pathname + url.search} />, {
      title: 'Aster App',
      revive: true,
      manifest,
    });
  },
};
```

Serve the client build and pass its Aster manifest to the SSR renderer. For a custom build supply `revivalUrl` and `runtimeUrl` or map both package names. SSR runs registered cleanup callbacks and preserves each router's own request URL and params. Tagged `html` templates also work in server components.

## Documentation
Island props can contain JSX children, client component exports, and named handlers exported from compiled client modules. An exported component can recreate locally captured handlers on activation. Keep request-only capabilities and private data on the server.
